newsitem.title: USA: Minn House committee rejects Twins stadium bill.
newsitem.headline: Minn House committee rejects Twins stadium bill.

text.p: A Minnesota House committee on Monday declined to advance a bill to fund a new stadium for the Minnesota Twins American League baseball club, a legislative aide said.

The state house tax committee first rejected plans to finance a stadium through cigarette tax hikes or expanded gambling and then further declined to approve a bill calling for a ticket buyout to tie the Twins to their lease in the Metrodome, legislative aide Gerrie Boice said.

The committee's decision makes approval of a ballpark an uphill battle, but has not killed the project yet, said Brian Dietz, spokesman for Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson, who supports plans for a new stadium.

"We certainly feel that without a new baseball stadium for the Twins they will leave Minnesota in the next couple of years," Dietz said. "They have the option after 1998 to exit their lease, which they can do if they are losing money and they have been and will be in the Metrodome."
Dietz said that "anything is still possible," and noted that other controversial bills have survived several rejections during a legislative session before being approved.
Boice said that the tax committee met four hours before determining that it could not pass a stadium proposal.
After initially taking no action on a bill sponsored by Rep. Ann Rest, D-New Hope, the committee voted 13-12 to substitute a ticket buyout proposal from Rep. Todd Van Dellen, R-Plymouth, Boice said.
House Majority Leader Ted Winter, D-Fulda, plans to introduce a bill in the planning and fiscal policy committee to study the importance of professional sports to the state, Boice said.
A Minnesota senate tax committee is scheduled to meet on stadium plans Monday afternoon.
Twins officials have estimated the cost of a retractable roof stadium at more than $400 million.

The team's lease runs through 2011, but includes an escape clause giving the Twins an out after the 1998 season if ticket sales are poor in relation to the rest of the league or if the ballclub loses money three years in a row.
Minnesota's legislature is scheduled to adjourn on May 19.
